card.title: The Man Who Sold His Dreams
card.premise: A tired man finds the shop that buys dreams and sells it his, one night at a time, until the shopkeeper asks for the oldest one.
card.human_emotion: The quiet grief of trading who you are for what you owe, and the relief of discovering it mattered to someone.
card.magical_element: A shop that buys dreams: selling them is what exhaustion feels like, trading away who you are one night at a time.
card.visual_anchor: Glass jars on endless shelves, each glowing with a tiny captured dream.
card.ending_image: A letter tucked beneath the old tree: Thank you. Keep this one.
card.lingering_question: What have I already sold to get through the month, and who was it really worth something to?
card.connection: The pilot: it opens Fann's lost-dreams thread. His sold dreams are out in the city, and one of them is being dreamed by a girl who can't sleep.

script.title: The Man Who Sold His Dreams
script.narration_direction: A legend told to one listener at 2 AM: low, warm, unhurried, close to the mic. Let every pause breathe, and give each loss its own silence. The Shopkeeper is kind and in no hurry; Fann is tired and quiet, his voice barely above the room. A faint smile only on the last line.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: They say a shop buys dreams at midnight.
lines.delivery: low and intimate, a secret told to one person

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Fann had two jobs, and letters he couldn't open.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: One midnight, a window glowed where there had always been a wall.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Inside, jars, each holding a dream.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then the tune he always hummed was gone.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then the shopkeeper asked for the oldest: a boy, a giant tree, a sea so blue it hurt.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She tilted a mirror. Across the city, a girl who couldn't sleep was dreaming them.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He left the money, and walked home with the last jar, humming.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That night, he dreamed of the tree. Beneath it, a letter.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It said: Thank you. Keep this one.
lines.delivery: barely above a whisper, a faint smile

script.closing_line: Some dreams are too old to sell.

characters.name: The Shopkeeper

locations.name: The Midnight Shop

shots.description: The legend in one image: a dream for sale, alone on a counter at midnight. The cover frame.

shots.video_prompt: the tiny sea inside the jar moves, the tree's leaves stir, dust motes drift through the amber glow
sfx: faint hum of the glowing jar

shots.description: Who he is: two jobs, letters he can't open. We hear his tune for the first time.

shots.video_prompt: rain trickles down the window, steam long gone from the tea, his shoulders rise and fall with one slow breath

shots.description: One midnight on the walk home: a glowing shop where a wall has always been.
shots.image_prompt: Wide shot of a narrow rain-soaked alley, a tiny old shopfront glowing amber squeezed between two dark buildings where no gap should be, Fann small in the foreground seen from behind, looking up at it
shots.video_prompt: rain falls steadily, puddles ripple, the shop window's warm light flickers gently
sfx: distant car on a wet road

shots.description: Inside: endless shelves of glowing jars, and the Shopkeeper, unhurried. Her moon bell rings as he steps in.
shots.image_prompt: Towering shelves of small glass jars, each glowing with a different tiny scene, the brass moon-shaped bell above the door still swaying, the Shopkeeper behind the counter polishing a jar with a half-smile
shots.video_prompt: jar lights pulse softly at different rhythms, the bell sways once and settles
sfx: low hum of the glowing jars

shots.description: He needs the money: how much for one?
shots.image_prompt: Medium shot across the counter, Fann standing at the worn wooden counter, one hand resting on the wood beside a small glowing jar, looking down at it, tired and hesitant, shelves of glowing jars rising into shadow behind him
shots.video_prompt: the jar's light pulses softly, dust motes drift, his shoulders rise with one slow breath
sfx: low hum of the glowing jars

shots.description: The sale, every night: a dream changes hands across the counter.
shots.image_prompt: Extreme close-up on the worn wooden counter: Fann's hand sliding a small glass jar toward the Shopkeeper's waiting hand, inside the jar a tiny swirl of glowing light like a captured dream, the round wall clock blurred behind them with its hands at 12:07
shots.video_prompt: the light inside the jar swirls slowly like smoke, dust motes drift through the amber glow, the hands barely move
sfx: glass jar set down on wood

shots.description: The first loss: dreamless nights, the colour draining out of his sleep.
shots.image_prompt: High angle, Fann asleep in his narrow bed with a blank, still face, the whole room drained to cool greys and blues, the desk lamp switched off, only faint streetlight through the rain-streaked window
shots.video_prompt: faint streetlight shifts across the blanket, the room otherwise perfectly still

shots.description: The second loss: his mornings, grey.
shots.image_prompt: Fann sitting on the edge of his narrow bed at dawn, elbows on his knees, staring at the floor, the whole room washed out to pale greys, cold flat light through the window, the desk lamp switched off
shots.video_prompt: pale light shifts slowly across the floor, dust hangs in the still air

shots.description: The third loss: he reaches for his tune, and it isn't there.
shots.image_prompt: Medium shot, Fann standing alone at the rain-streaked window at night, one hand pressed flat to his chest, lips slightly parted as if about to hum, his reflection faint in the dark glass, the room behind him dim
shots.video_prompt: rain runs down the glass, his reflection wavers, he barely moves

shots.description: The oldest dream, the brightest image in the episode: a boy, a giant tree, a sea so blue it hurt.
shots.image_prompt: A small boy in an oversized mustard scarf standing beneath the enormous old tree on the cliff, looking out at the sea, wind in the grass
shots.video_prompt: clouds drift, waves roll in far below, leaves and grass sway in the wind, the boy's scarf flutters

shots.description: This one pays for everything. Fann, afraid: where do they go?
shots.image_prompt: Close-up, Fann's face lit warm gold from below as the Shopkeeper holds up the oldest jar between them, inside it a tiny bright summer scene, Fann's eyes wide, wet and hesitant
shots.video_prompt: the jar's glow brightens slowly, reflections tremble in Fann's eyes
sfx: jar glow swelling into a soft hum

shots.description: The mirror shows where his dreams went: a room far across the city.
shots.image_prompt: Close-up of a small round brass hand mirror standing alone on the worn wooden counter, tilted toward the viewer, no people anywhere in the frame; in its glass, instead of a reflection, a dark lamp-lit bedroom far across the city with someone asleep in a narrow bed
shots.video_prompt: a faint shimmer ripples across the mirror's surface, the far lamp flickers once

shots.video_prompt: light rain, reflections shimmer on the pavement, the jar's glow sways with his steps

shots.description: That night he dreams of the tree again.

shots.video_prompt: grass ripples in the wind, cloud shadows slide across the cliff

shots.description: The final image: a letter left for him beneath the old tree.

canon.summary: Fann, worn out by two jobs and letters he couldn't open, found the Midnight Shop one midnight where a wall had always been, and sold the Shopkeeper his dreams one night at a time. He lost his dreaming nights, the colour of his mornings and the tune he always hummed. When she asked for his oldest dream, a mirror showed him a girl across the city dreaming his sold dreams and smiling; he left the money, kept the last one and walked home humming.
changes: Fann has sold most of his dreams to the Shopkeeper; he kept only the oldest one: a boy, a giant tree, a sea so blue it hurt
Selling them cost him his dreaming nights, the colour of his mornings and, for a while, his three-note tune; with the last jar he hums it again
Fann's sold dreams are being dreamed by others across the city, including a girl who couldn't sleep; her face was never shown and she was never named
Someone left Fann a letter beneath the Old Tree in his dream: Thank you. Keep this one.
Fann knows the Midnight Shop and its moon-shaped bell
